chunks: From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about two partners; if one of them testified for his partner, he said: 'His testimony is valid, except in a matter in which he has a share.'
ai.seo_question: Is a partner's testimony valid in Islamic law when dealing with another partner?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal principle of 'shahadatu al-sharik' (partner's testimony), establishing that while a partner is generally admissible as a witness for the other, their testimony is voided in specific matters where they hold a direct financial stake, thereby preventing bias. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on ensuring impartiality in commercial transactions and is foundational in the chapter of evidences (al-Bayinat) within Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*.
